scope: Compare current official Enygma Public documentation with the historical testnet transaction 0x09edab2b...25bb. Documentation statements are official claims, not independent proof of historical transaction behavior.

sources.title: How Enygma Public works

relevant_claims.claim: A relayer submits Enygma Public transactions and charges gas in RLS.
For a shielded payment, the wallet proves a smaller payment of gas from the sender's shielded RLS to the relayer; for an RLS payment, the relayer fee can instead be a note in the same proof.
The documentation describes the relayer checking its fee and submitting the payment and fee payment in one transaction through Multicall3.
Each gas fee includes a 15% commission to the Rayls Foundation; the relayer collects fees and pays the Foundation share after the transaction is mined.
The shared vault accepts any ERC-20 token in one Merkle tree, so a payment in that shared vault does not publicly identify which token was moved.

sources.title: Enygma Public

relevant_claims.claim: The deployment's auditor can read shielded payments; the public does not see who paid whom or how much.
Enygma Public transactions pay gas in RLS through a relayer.

The documented deployment includes vault contracts, a verifier, a gas forwarder, a relayer, and an owner multisig; the owner multisig can upgrade the registry and shared vault, register vaults, and add verifying keys.

relevant_claims.claim: The general Rayls Public Chain gas token is USDr, while Enygma Public is documented as an exception: its transactions pay gas in RLS through a relayer, with a 15% commission to the Rayls Foundation.

consistent_with_current_documentation.observation: The examined transaction is submitted from a relayer address.
consistent_with_current_documentation.assessment: consistent; it does not by itself establish the relayer's internal fee accounting.

consistent_with_current_documentation.observation: The transaction receipt has one input and three outputs.
consistent_with_current_documentation.assessment: consistent with the current source-level PaymentRelayerFee layout and the documented possibility that an RLS payment includes the relayer fee note in the same proof; historical circuit semantics are not proven.

consistent_with_current_documentation.observation: A separate transaction with an observed value of 0.576 RLS occurs four blocks later.
consistent_with_current_documentation.assessment: temporally consistent with the documentation's statement that the relayer pays the Foundation share after mining; the recipient identity and transaction purpose remain unverified, so this is not proof of the documented commission payment.

consistent_with_current_documentation.observation: The destination is identified in current Explorer metadata as SharedVaultProxy.
consistent_with_current_documentation.assessment: consistent with the documented shared-vault design; the token type remains unidentifiable from this transaction alone.

apparent_difference_or_gap.observation: The historical transaction calls transferV2 directly on SharedVaultProxy; the saved transaction record says it is not routed through Multicall3.
apparent_difference_or_gap.documentation_claim: The current documentation describes submitting the payment and fee payment together through Multicall3.
apparent_difference_or_gap.assessment: unresolved. Possible explanations include different transaction paths, an RLS-payment fee-note variant, or a documentation/code version difference. Do not assume one explanation.

fee_arithmetic_without_semantic_assumpti.limitation: The relationship does not establish that statement[8] is denominated in RLS, that the related transfer is the Foundation commission for this transaction, or that 3.84 is the relayer's retained fee.

official_claims: Current Rayls documentation states that Enygma Public gas is charged in RLS through a relayer.
Current Rayls documentation states that an Enygma Public fee includes a 15% Rayls Foundation commission.
Current Rayls documentation states that an RLS payment may include the relayer fee as a note in the same proof.
Current Rayls documentation states that the relayer collects fees and pays the Foundation share after the transaction is mined.
direct_observations_from_existing_transa: The historical transaction is a direct transferV2 call to SharedVaultProxy, from the relayer address.
The decoded receipt contains one input, three outputs, and ten statement integers.
A separate transaction four blocks later was previously recorded with a value of 0.576 RLS; its purpose and beneficiary identity are unresolved.
inferences_not_upgraded: The historical statement[8] is an RLS-denominated fee.
The 0.576 RLS transfer is the Foundation commission associated with this shielded payment.
The 3.84 arithmetic remainder is the relayer's retained fee.
The third output note belongs to the relayer.
unknowns: Whether the current documentation describes the exact version and transaction path active on 2026-11-21.
Whether the historical transfer was denominated in RLS or another token without independent token/vault identification.
Whether the related 0.576 RLS transaction is the fee payment described by current documentation.
Why the examined historical transaction is a direct vault call whereas current documentation describes Multicall3 for a payment-plus-fee submission path.
